title: Processing of identified data at source
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) processes and transmits identified data including student ID, course, file reference, and requesting role to the Assignment & Grading Service.
assumptions: Student ID is a unique identifier that can identify the data subject.

title: Identifier transmitted in data flow
description: Student ID is transmitted as part of the data flow from P1 to P2, providing a unique reference to the identity of the data subject.
assumptions: Student ID is a globally unique identifier within the educational system.

title: Linking through unique identifier in data flow
description: The student ID transmitted in the data flow can be used to link data across systems and identify the specific student associated with the submission and grading request.
assumptions: Student ID is unique and can be correlated across different data flows and systems.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in data flow
description: The combination of student ID, course, and file reference can serve as quasi-identifiers that may allow linking or re-identification of individuals when combined with other available data.
assumptions: The combination of these attributes may be unique or near-unique to specific students within the context.

title: Data propagation to another service
description: Personal data (student ID, course, file reference, requesting role) is propagated from the Grades Portal Web App to the Assignment & Grading Service, expanding the scope of data exposure.
assumptions: The Assignment & Grading Service may have different security controls or access policies than the portal.

title: Data shared with predetermined set of parties
description: Personal data is shared with the Assignment & Grading Service, which is a predetermined and static set of parties known at design time.
assumptions: The Assignment & Grading Service is a known, fixed recipient of the data flow.

title: Unawareness of data processing by data subject
description: Students may not be fully aware that their submission and grading data (including student ID, course, file reference) is being transmitted to and processed by the Assignment & Grading Service.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate all data flows and processing activities.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the quality of privacy notices and user awareness.

title: Lack of control over data processing preferences
description: Students may lack control over how their personal data is processed and shared with the Assignment & Grading Service, with limited ability to set preferences or opt-out.
assumptions: The system may not provide granular consent options for data sharing.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the system's consent and preference mechanisms.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The data flow includes multiple data elements (student ID, course, file reference, requesting role) that may be more than strictly necessary for the functional purpose of routing submission and grading requests.
assumptions: Some of these data elements may be collectable or processable in a more minimal way.
uncertainty_note: Depends on functional requirements and whether all data elements are strictly necessary.

title: Teacher identity linked through unique login identifier
description: Teacher logs in using a unique identifier (username, email, or institutional ID) that links their identity to the submission queue they request, enabling correlation of their actions with their personal identity.
assumptions: Teacher authentication uses a unique identifier that persists across sessions

title: Submission data quasi-identifiers enable linking
description: The submission queue data may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., course name, submission timestamp, assignment type) that, when combined, could link submissions to specific students or teachers.
assumptions: Submission metadata contains multiple attributes that could be combined for re-identification

title: Processing of identified teacher and student data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified information including teacher identity and student submission data, which are directly linked to identifiable individuals.
assumptions: System stores and processes data with direct identifiers

title: Unique identifiers in submission data
description: Submission records contain unique references to student identity (e.g., student ID, username) that allow identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Student submissions are associated with unique student identifiers

title: Observable communications reveal teacher activity
description: Teacher's login attempts, submission queue requests, and interactions with the Grades Portal are observable communications that could be monitored or logged.
assumptions: System logs all user interactions and communications

title: System responses reveal data availability
description: System responses to teacher requests (e.g., queue lists, submission counts) reveal what data exists and is accessible, potentially exposing information about which students have submitted work.
assumptions: System responses include metadata about data availability

title: Potentially sensitive data collected beyond functional need
description: The system may collect or process more sensitive data types than strictly required for the teacher to review submissions (e.g., full student names, detailed metadata).
assumptions: Data collection scope exceeds minimum requirements for grade review functionality

title: Unnecessary data analysis and enrichment
description: Submission data may be analyzed, enriched, or transformed beyond what is needed for the teacher to perform their review function (e.g., generating analytics, cross-referencing with other systems).
assumptions: System performs additional processing beyond basic queue display

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Submission data may be accessible to or shared with a predetermined set of parties (e.g., administrators, other teachers, support staff) beyond what is functionally necessary for the teacher's review task.
assumptions: Data access is granted to multiple internal parties

title: Students unaware of data processing for review
description: Students may not be aware that their submission data is being processed, stored, and made accessible to teachers for review purposes.
assumptions: Students lack clear notification about data processing activities

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: Students may have limited ability to set preferences or consent regarding how their submission data is processed, stored, and shared with teachers.
assumptions: Data subject consent mechanisms are limited or absent

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than is actually needed for the teacher to review submissions (e.g., collecting full student profiles when only submission metadata is required).
assumptions: Data collection exceeds functional requirements for grade review

title: Potential invalid consent for data processing
description: Student data processing for submission review may not rely on valid consent, particularly if consent is bundled or not properly informed.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not meet regulatory requirements

title: Student names used as unique identifiers for linking
description: Student names in the submission data can serve as unique identifiers that allow linking this data to other records or systems, potentially enabling cross-referencing of student information across different contexts.
assumptions: Teacher or third party has access to other student records that could be linked via name

title: Quasi-identifier combination through student attributes
description: Combination of student names, work content, and submission times could serve as quasi-identifiers that, when combined with other available data, could uniquely identify students and link their academic performance data.
assumptions: Teacher or system has access to additional student data that could be combined with this flow's data

title: Profiling of individual students through work patterns
description: Analysis of work content and submission times could enable profiling of individual students, revealing patterns in their academic behavior, performance trends, or learning habits.
assumptions: Teacher or system performs analysis on submission data to derive insights about individual students

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The system explicitly processes and displays identified student information (names, work content) to the teacher, making student identities directly visible in the data flow.
assumptions: Student names are included in the data transmitted to the teacher

title: Student names as direct identifiers
description: Student names in the submission data contain unique references to the identity of the data subject, enabling direct identification of individual students.
assumptions: Student names are unique identifiers within the educational context

title: Revealing attributes through work content and submission times
description: Work content and submission times reveal attributes about students including their academic performance, work habits, and potentially sensitive information about their learning process.
assumptions: Work content may contain personal or sensitive information; submission times reveal behavioral patterns

title: Potentially sensitive student work content disclosed
description: Student work content may contain sensitive personal information that is disclosed to the teacher beyond what is strictly necessary for grade evaluation purposes.
assumptions: Work content may include personal reflections, sensitive topics, or information beyond academic requirements

title: Data shared with predetermined set of parties
description: Student submission data is made accessible to teachers, a predetermined and static set of parties, which may be broader than functionally necessary for the grading process.
assumptions: Teachers have access to student data that may not be strictly required for their role

title: Student unawareness of data sharing with teachers
description: Students may not be aware that their submission data, including work content and submission times, is being shared with teachers through this portal.
assumptions: Students lack clear notification or consent mechanisms regarding data sharing

title: Lack of student control over data sharing preferences
description: Students may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their submission data is shared with teachers and what information is disclosed.
assumptions: No mechanism exists for students to opt-out or customize data sharing

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data (work content, submission times) than is actually needed for the functional goal of displaying grades and submissions to teachers.
assumptions: Some data elements may be more granular than necessary for the intended purpose

title: Linking through unique student identifier
description: Student's unique identifier (e.g., student ID, email) is used to link their identity to their grades and feedback data, enabling tracking across systems.
assumptions: Student identifiers are collected and used to authenticate and retrieve grades.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Grades and feedback data may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., course names, grade levels, timestamps) that can be combined to re-identify students even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: Grades data includes contextual information that can be combined for identification.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system processes identified student data (grades and feedback) that directly links to the student's identity.
assumptions: Grades portal stores and processes student-specific grade records.

title: Processing of identifier data
description: Student identifiers are processed to retrieve and display grades, creating a direct link between identity and academic performance data.
assumptions: Student authentication requires identifier verification.

title: Detection through application side effects
description: System responses (e.g., loading times, error messages, available courses) may reveal information about the student's grade status or academic standing.
assumptions: System behavior may inadvertently disclose information about grades.

title: Collection of sensitive data types
description: Grades and feedback are sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is strictly necessary for the student to view their own grades.
assumptions: Grades are considered sensitive academic performance data.

title: Unnecessary data treatment and analysis
description: Grades data may be analyzed, enriched, or transformed (e.g., for analytics, reporting) beyond what is needed for the student to view their grades.
assumptions: Grades portal may perform additional processing on grade data.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware of how their grades data is collected, processed, stored, or potentially shared beyond the grades portal.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not fully disclose all data processing activities.

title: Lack of control over data processing preferences
description: Students may have limited ability to set preferences or consent regarding how their grades data is processed, stored, or shared.
assumptions: Grades portal may not offer granular consent controls for grade data.

title: Lack of control over data access
description: Students may not have full control over who can access their grades data (e.g., parents, administrators, third parties).
assumptions: Grades data may be accessible to multiple parties beyond the student.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Grades data may be processed beyond what is functionally needed for the student to view their own grades (e.g., for analytics, research, or administrative purposes).
assumptions: Grades data may be used for purposes beyond student grade retrieval.

title: Sensitive grade data disclosed
description: Grades are sensitive personal data that should only be disclosed when strictly required. The portal displays grades to students, which may be more sensitive than functionally necessary for the display functionality.

title: Fine-grained grade data disclosed
description: The granularity of grade data (e.g., specific scores, letter grades, teacher comments) may be more detailed than needed for the student to view their own academic performance.

title: Unnecessary data treatment
description: The system may be analyzing, enriching, or transforming grade data beyond what is necessary for simply displaying grades to the student.

title: Excessive party exposure
description: Grade data is made accessible to the student (predetermined party), but there may be additional parties (e.g., administrators, teachers) with access beyond what is functionally necessary for the student viewing their own grades.

title: Lack of student control over preferences
description: Students may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their grade data is processed, stored, or disclosed within the portal system.

title: Lack of data subject access control
description: Students may lack full control over accessing their own grade data, including limitations on when, how, or in what format they can retrieve their information.

title: GDPR data minimization violation
description: The system may process more personal data (grades, teacher feedback) than is actually needed for the functional goal of displaying grades to students, violating the data minimization principle.

title: Lawfulness problems not related to consent
description: Processing of student grade data may have lawfulness issues not related to consent, such as incorrect lawful ground for processing or automated decision-making on sensitive personal data.

title: Linking through parent-child account identifiers
description: Parent account is linked to child account, enabling linking of parent's access to child's educational data through unique identifier relationships.
assumptions: Parent-child account linkage is implemented in the system

title: Quasi-identifier combining parent and child data
description: Combination of parent account information with child grades can serve as quasi-identifiers that may link data across different contexts.
assumptions: Parent-child relationship data is stored and processed

title: Processing of identified parent and child data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified information including parent account credentials and child's grade records.
assumptions: System stores and processes identifiable account and grade data

title: Unique identifier in parent account data
description: Parent account contains unique references to the parent's identity that can be used to identify the data subject.
assumptions: Parent accounts use unique identifiers (username, email, etc.)

title: Quasi-identifier through parent-child relationship
description: The combination of parent account with child grades creates quasi-identifying information that may allow identification of specific individuals.
assumptions: Parent-child relationship is stored and can be used for identification

title: Sensitive grade data collection
description: Grades are sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is strictly necessary for the parent's access request.
assumptions: Grade data is considered sensitive educational information

title: Potential unnecessary data treatment
description: The system may analyze or process grade data in ways that extend beyond the functional goal of displaying grades to the parent.
assumptions: System may perform additional processing on grade data
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if additional processing occurs beyond display

title: Data accessible to predetermined parties
description: Grade data is made accessible to the parent (predetermined party), which may be more than functionally necessary if child's consent is not obtained.
assumptions: Parent has access to child's grades through account linkage

title: Child unawareness of grade access
description: The child data subject may not be aware that their grades are being accessed and displayed to the parent through the account linkage.
assumptions: Child is a separate data subject from the parent

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: The child may lack control over how their grade data is processed, shared with parent, or retained in the system.
assumptions: Child has limited or no control over parent's access to their data

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing of child's grade data by parent may exceed what is actually needed, potentially violating data minimization requirements.
assumptions: GDPR or similar regulations apply to this educational data processing
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific regulatory context and consent mechanisms

title: Potential invalid consent for child data access
description: Parent's access to child's grades may not rely on valid consent from the child or appropriate legal basis.
assumptions: Child is a separate data subject requiring consent for data access
uncertainty_note: Depends on age of child and consent mechanisms in place

title: Unique identifier linking in grade records
description: Grade records contain unique student identifiers that can be used to link data across systems and contexts.
assumptions: Student IDs are unique and can be correlated with other data sources

title: Quasi-identifier combination in grade data
description: Combination of student ID, course, grade, and date can serve as quasi-identifiers that may link to other datasets.
assumptions: Multiple attributes in grade records can be combined to identify individuals

title: Profiling through grade data analysis
description: Grade records can be analyzed to create performance profiles of students, potentially revealing patterns about learning abilities.
assumptions: Grade data can be aggregated and analyzed for pattern recognition

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The grading service processes grade records that contain identified student information.
assumptions: Grade records contain direct identifiers for students

title: Unique identifier in grade records
description: Grade records contain unique references to student identity through student IDs.
assumptions: Student IDs are unique identifiers within the system

title: Revealing attributes in grade data
description: Grade records reveal academic performance attributes that can support identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Academic performance is a revealing attribute that can identify students

title: Sensitive grade data collection
description: Grade data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required.
assumptions: Grade records contain sensitive academic performance information

title: Data propagation to multiple parties
description: Grade data is accessible to students, parents, and teachers - multiple parties beyond functional necessity.
assumptions: Different views are created for different user groups

title: Excessive party exposure to grade data
description: Personal data is made accessible to more parties (students, parents, teachers) than functionally necessary.
assumptions: Multiple stakeholder groups require access to grade information

title: Unawareness of grade data processing
description: Students and parents may not be fully aware of how their grade data is collected, processed, and shared.
assumptions: Users may not understand the full scope of data processing

title: Lack of data subject control over preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control over how their grade data is processed, stored, and shared.
assumptions: Limited user control mechanisms for data processing preferences

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Grade data may be processed beyond what is actually needed for the functional goals of the system.
assumptions: Some grade data processing may exceed functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific implementation and data retention policies
